subtitles.en: I'm on the side of the people who say we need these open source models, great, unregulated open source models, crazy idea, crazy crazy idea.
subtitles.zh: 我支持那些主张开源模型的人，认为需要不受监管的开源模型，这想法很疯狂。

subtitles.en: And so basically you got to figure out a way to regulate, it's not like open source closed source, US, China, it's regulated, unregulated is the important thing here, if you
subtitles.zh: 关键是要找到监管方式，不是开源闭源或中美之分，而是监管与不监管的区别。

subtitles.en: believe it's dangerous. If you don't for some reason think it's screwdriver, it's the screwdriver is going around committing crimes.
subtitles.zh: 如果你认为它危险。如果你不这么想，那就像螺丝刀在犯罪一样。

subtitles.en: I would have a different view of screwdriver, it ain't a screwdriver.
subtitles.zh: 我对螺丝刀的看法会不同，但它不是螺丝刀。

subtitles.en: It's going around capable of doing things that you and I wouldn't do, that's a big difference and we have to reckon with it whether it's closed or open source.
subtitles.zh: 它能做你我不会做的事，这是巨大区别，无论开源闭源都必须面对。

subtitles.en: Hello and welcome to another episode of the AdLots podcast.
subtitles.zh: 欢迎收听AdLots播客新一期节目。

subtitles.en: I'm Joe Wasimble. And I'm Tracy Alley. Tracy, no shortage of AI news, is it?
subtitles.zh: 我是Joe Wasimble。我是Tracy Alley。Tracy，AI新闻真不少。

subtitles.en: No, it feels like everything is AI, it's just AI all over.
subtitles.zh: 是啊，感觉一切都是AI，到处都是AI。

subtitles.en: No, it is, you know, I really like all the other stuff that we talk about, I love talk about the Fed, talk about oil, home building, all of that stuff.
subtitles.zh: 没错，我真的很喜欢我们聊的其他话题，比如美联储、石油、住宅建设等。

subtitles.en: niche markets. Yeah, I love it. And I want to do it forever.
subtitles.zh: 小众市场。是的，我喜欢，我想一直做下去。

subtitles.en: It does feel like, since, you know, Chad GPT came out, if you probably plotted a chart, the percentage of our episodes that are in some way connected to AI, keep going up, maybe
subtitles.zh: 确实感觉，自从ChatGPT问世以来，如果画个图表，我们节目中与AI相关的比例一直在上升，也许

subtitles.en: even exponentially up like many AI charts.
subtitles.zh: 甚至像许多AI图表那样呈指数级增长。

clip_research.source_claim: The important AI regulatory divide is not open source versus closed source or US versus China, but regulated versus unregulated, because frontier AI is not a mere tool like a screwdriver and can act in ways humans would not.
clip_research.public_baseline: Public coverage of the same Bloomberg Odd Lots interview confirms Greg Jensen, Bridgewater co-CIO, argued AI poses real human extinction risk and that regulation may only arrive after AI causes human casualties, comparing the moment to February 2020 pre-pandemic complacency.
clip_research.surprise_gap: A major hedge fund's co-CIO, whose firm was an early backer of OpenAI and Anthropic, publicly frames frontier AI as an existential threat and calls for regulation rather than defending an unregulated open-source position, which cuts against the usual industry posture of incumbents with AI exposure.

evidence.fact: Speaker says the key distinction is regulated versus unregulated, not open versus closed source or US versus China, and that AI is not a screwdriver.

winning_patterns: 机构/人物权威 + 具体数字/资产 + 强问题，例如 高盛王逸：4-5万亿城市更新会拖住楼市吗
大机构/名人 + 被逼/陷阱/真相/转向 等张力词，例如 野村辜朝明：日本央行被逼到墙角
具体数据 + 政策动作疑问，例如 6月PMI释放积极信号，政府会加码吗
反常识判断 + 下一步条件，例如 低估值可能是价值陷阱，需等待政策转向消费
中国相关议题更容易获得点击，但表达要落在政策、需求、信心、估值、产业升级这些正向框架

让观众产生单一强反应：居然如此、终于有人说、他说的是真的吗、原来中国优势在这里
大实话角度来自表达者身份与观点反差；言行反差角度必须有公开动作或披露支撑
